By now everyone has heard the conspiracy of a one world currency. 

It’s very real. Let me ease you into the rabbit hole.

In 1996, a proposal for a United Future World Currency begins taking shape.

In 2000, the trademark “Eurodollar” is registered.

In July 2009, prototype “United Future World Currency” coins are placed into the hands of G8 leaders. One is even held up by Russia’s president during a press conference and called a symbol of unity.

Then… enter Bitcoin.

The story we’re told is that Bitcoin was created to fight centralized money.

But what if that was the only narrative capable of getting a global currency adopted?

Imagine this:

Every previous attempt at a supranational currency failed because it came from governments, institutions, and central banks. People rejected the messenger before they even considered the idea.

So the next attempt took the opposite approach.

No central issuer.

No headquarters.

No CEO.

No government.

Instead of convincing “governments” first, you convince millions of individuals.

Instead of calling it a “world currency,” you call it decentralized money.

Twenty years later, the outcome is remarkably similar:

 A massive amount of Bitcoin is centralized in one wallet.

 A single monetary network that ignores national borders, trades 24/7 across nearly every country, and settles value without asking permission.
